blocks.text: Data duplication refers to the presence of one or more identical copies of data, either intentionally or unintentionally, in different locations in an organization’s infrastructure. You can remove duplicate copies to reduce your attack surface, and track the source from where the sensitive data originated and its presence in different files.

DSPM scans the data stores and detects duplicate files across cloud, SaaS, and on-premises environments. This allows you to validate and delete the extra copies to limit the exposure of data to unauthorized users and protect sensitive data.
The Data Duplications page has the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: View all the duplicate copies of files and tables in the data stores.
View DLP engines and dictionaries that were triggered to detect duplicate files and tables.
Remove duplicate data to save on storage, backup, and operational costs.
Reduce the possibility of users creating duplicate files.
Delete potentially outdated data.

blocks.text: On the Data Duplications page (Data Security > DSPM > Data Duplications), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Apply filters to view specific information.
Add additional filters.
View the list of duplicate files. For each file copy you can see:
File Path: The location where the file exists. Click to view the details.
Details: The file properties.
Evidence: Validate the findings and view trigger data along with the last scan. This tab is displayed only if evidence collection option is enabled and configured prior to the scan.

Data duplications: Duplicate file copies. Click File Path to view the file details on the Details tab or click Resource Name to view the resource inventory graph, sensitive data available in the resource, or alerts generated for the resource.
File access: The users that accessed the file in the last 7 days.
Copies: The total number of file copies detected, including the original file. Click the number to view the duplicate copies.
See image.
DLP Engines : The DLP engines that match the files.
DLP Dictionaries: The DLP dictionaries that match the files.
Document Types: The document type that matches the files.
Hash: The file’s MD5 sum.
File Size: The size of the file in kilobytes (KB).
Total Size: The total size of all the file copies.
File Type: The file type (e.g., txt).
No. of Regions: The number of regions where the duplicate file copies are found.
No. of Accounts: The number of cloud accounts in which duplicate file copies are found.
Clouds: The cloud service provider in which the duplicate file copies are found.
Export the data and download the report as an Excel file by selecting one of the following options from the Export drop-down menu:

Summary View: This report is based on the current page view, including applied filters and visible columns. This report summarizes the total number of duplicate files and their locations across accounts and regions, identified by unique file hashes.
Full View: This report lists all duplicate file instances and their attributes. This report allows you to know the exact location of each duplicate file instance.

The Full View report is generated as a ZIP file, which can contain up to 10 files with a maximum of 50,000 rows each. Use report filters to select and view specific data and stay within the 500,000-row limit.

Show or hide columns in the table.
